findings.claim: The EPK's behaviour when a credit is not yet confirmed in domain 02 is specified as two different products — a hard block on the EPK and a claimed-badge render — and a third signal (the Blocked state) argues against the second, with no marker deferring the choice.
findings.evidence: 21.09-campaign-press-kit-epk.md:63 (Edge Cases) — 'Credits not yet confirmed in 02 | The EPK cannot claim credits the credit graph has not confirmed … | Blocked on the unconfirmed credit, with a link to 02. **Or** included as **claimed**, visibly distinguished. Never silently rendered as verified'. 21.09-campaign-press-kit-epk.md:79 (States) — 'Blocked | Credits unconfirmed in 02 | Named blocker; the alternative is claiming what we cannot verify' — which rejects the claimed option the edge row permits. 21.09-campaign-press-kit-epk.md:116 (D-03) — 'Unverified credits are blocked or marked claimed, never rendered as verified'. No open question in the file covers the choice: Q-01 is polymorphism, Q-02 leak control, Q-03 photo licences, Q-04 provenance rendering.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent whether an unconfirmed credit blocks EPK creation/sharing outright or renders inside the EPK with a claimed badge. The two produce different products: one gates the artist's send on another domain's state, the other ships a weaker document. The States table's Blocked row and D-03's disjunction point opposite ways, so no default can be read off the text.

findings.claim: A `Decayed` coverage item has no defined rendered strength, even though the EPK is required to render exactly one of three strengths per item and badge decay is required to propagate into every EPK that embedded the quote.
findings.evidence: 21.07-coverage-clipping-log.md:92 (States) — 'Decayed | Source link rotted | Verification lapses; the artist is told before the EPK quietly weakens'. The three renderable strengths are closed: 21.09-campaign-press-kit-epk.md:44 — 'The EPK renders the strength 21.07 computed — `verified` / `verified-at-timestamp` / `claimed`'. The only decay target stated is class-bound to playlist adds: 21.07-coverage-clipping-log.md:81 — 'Add stays in the log, badge decays toward claimed unless a snapshot was captured', while 21.07:90 defines verified-at-timestamp by artefact class — 'Live but mutable source confirmed (playlist add)'. Propagation is mandatory: promotion-marketing-cx.md:187-189 — 'Badge decay — a verified link that later rots — must propagate to every EPK that embedded the quote, or the EPK asserts a verification it can no longer stand behind.'
findings.forcedInvention: For a rotted *article* (the `verified` class), an implementer must invent whether the EPK now shows `claimed`, shows `verified-at-timestamp` (which the taxonomy reserves for mutable playlist sources), or shows a fourth 'decayed' label the closed three-value vocabulary does not contain.

findings.claim: The domain CX file lists `PAYOLA_DISCLOSURE_REQUIRED` as a block verdict, while the owning feature defines it as an allow-with-obligation verdict — the same code cannot both block a spend and let it proceed.
findings.evidence: promotion-marketing-cx.md:142-144 (CX-03 synthesis Q2) — 'Trigger chain: `offer/pitch composed` → classifier evaluates → {allow | allow-with-disclosure | block (PAYOLA_AIRPLAY_BLOCKED / PAYOLA_DISCLOSURE_REQUIRED)}. Sync, blocking.' 21.05.03-payola-guardrail.md:40 (classification table) — 'Attention + endorsement (paid creator post, sponsored review, paid testimonial) | **Allowed with mandatory disclosure** | `PAYOLA_DISCLOSURE_REQUIRED` | A material connection exists; the audience must be told. Obligation attached, non-removable'. The CX list also omits `PAYOLA_PLACEMENT_BLOCKED`, the code that actually blocks the playlist-placement case CX-03 is about.
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer wiring the 21.02 send path from CX-03 would reject a paid-creator-post offer that the owning classifier allows with a label. The tree's ownership convention (CX-03 §1: 'the payola policy is owned solely by 21.05.03') resolves it, which is why this is a warning rather than blocking — but the CX statement is live, unmarked and wrong.

The behaviours differ for the exact abuse the feature exists to prevent.

findings.claim: Two adjacent edge rows require opposite uniqueness rules for embargoes on the same content, and the embargo object as defined has no scope field that would let both hold.

findings.claim: The small-n suppression rule that prevents re-identification of another artist's rejection history has no threshold value and no question owning one, while the file's own analysis shows the number is the whole protection.
findings.evidence: 21.03.01-media-target-directory.md:60 — 'Small-n response rate (target received 3 pitches total) | The statistic is noise and, worse, re-identifiable | Suppressed below a threshold. "Not enough data" beats a 33% that is one artist's outcome exposed'; :96 (D-02) — 'Small-n statistics are suppressed | Below threshold a response rate is both noise and re-identifiable.' The re-identification mechanism is spelled out but not bounded: 21.03-pitch-targets-crm-cx.md:34 — 'small-n targets make re-identification trivial (if a curator received 3 pitches this month, a 33% response rate identifies a specific artist's outcome to anyone who knows two of them)'. findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent the suppression n (and whether it is a count of pitches, of distinct senders, or a per-window figure) — the single parameter that decides whether the directory leaks an identifiable artist's rejection.

findings.claim: The live edge-case and state rows say off-platform ticketing means no sales data and no loop at all, while the resolved questions in the same files say external counts are ingested or attested as the normal case and the feature must be specified degraded-first — and the sub-domain's own rationale still rests on the superseded premise.
findings.evidence: Live rows: 21.08.02-geo-date-promotion-soft-seat.md:59 — 'Ticketing is off-platform | No sales data, no detection, no loop | The loop simply does not exist for that date'; :77 (States) — 'Not assessable | Off-platform ticketing | No data, no loop — stated, not faked'. Resolved rows: 21.08.02:109 — '**RESOLVED — a minority, and domain 19 states it as its own working assumption** … "Most shows on the platform — especially early on, and possibly forever — will be sold by DICE, Eventbrite, Ticketmaster …" … detection's normal input is an ingested or attested count of stated provenance and freshness … The "Ticketing is off-platform → no data, no loop" edge case above is the *no-connector, no-attestation* case, not every off-platform date'; 21.08.03-ticket-sale-attribution.md:108 — 'That makes **D-04 the default path rather than the exception** … this feature must therefore be specified degraded-first, with the true-attribution case as the better sub-case.' The uncorrected premise: 21.08-event-tour-marketing-index.md:11-12 — 'the attribution that — uniquely in this platform — actually works, because we own the transaction'; 21.08-event-tour-marketing-cx.md:10 — 'This is the only closed marketing loop in the platform … so "did the boost work?" has a real answer here'; and 21.08.03's Overview, Behavior, Happy Path and States all present the completed join as the primary path with 'Degraded' as an edge state. The domain's own correction convention forbids this: 21.07-coverage-clipping-log.md:101-104 — 'Wording superseded by a later owner ratification is **never deleted and never left standing unmarked**.'
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must decide whether soft-seat detection and ticket attribution are built join-first (with off-platform dates unassessable) or ingestion-first over provenance-and-freshness-stamped external counts. The two produce different primary surfaces, different empty states, and a different answer to whether the sub-domain's headline claim holds for most dates.

notableStrengths: 21.02.06 (pitch rate limits) and 21.05.03 (payola guardrail) are the two [DEEP] files and are effectively unambiguous: every threshold is a number with a unit and a rolling window, every verdict has a code, fail-closed semantics are stated three ways, and the last-slot race, sybil evasion, opt-out sabotage and free-text gaming cases all have specified outcomes.

The re-target convention on open questions is applied with unusual rigour: most rows state which stage has already run, why it did not close the question, which sibling rows are the same decision, and what is enforced in the interim.

The DQ-20.1 / DQ-20.3 correction pass (verification strength = artefact class + retrievability; provenance is a log state, never rendered) is propagated consistently across promotion-marketing-index.md D-02/D-08/D-09, promotion-marketing-cx.md CX-05/CX-08, 21.07 D-06/D-07 and 21.09 D-05, with both superseded wordings preserved under an explicit correction convention.
